statement: Show that $x^{4}-5x^{3}+5x^{2}+5x-6$ is divisible by $x^{2}-4x+3$, and find the other quadratic factor.
solution: Since $x^{2}-4x+3=(x-1)(x-3)$ and the quartic vanishes at $x=1$ and $x=3$, it is divisible. Let the other factor be $x^{2}+mx+n$. Then $(x^{2}-4x+3)(x^{2}+mx+n)=x^{4}+(m-4)x^{3}+(n-4m+3)x^{2}+(3m-4n)x+3n$. Matching gives $m-4=-5\\Rightarrow m=-1$; $3n=-6\\Rightarrow n=-2$; and the $x^{2}$ coefficient $n-4m+3=-2+4+3=5$ checks. So the other factor is $x^{2}-x-2$.
